title: Fragment sentinel and spillgate backpressure for tenant-aware evictor
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: In mixed multi-tenant workloads we observed high KV cache fragmentation that drove frequent cold spills and long-tail latency spikes during peak bursts. This PR introduces two coordinated subsystems: a lightweight Fragment Sentinel scanner that maintains a continuously-updated fragmentation map with low overhead and a Spillgate backpressure controller that gates spill initiation based on tenant residency budgets and runtime pressure signals. Design summary: The Fragment Sentinel performs incremental, jittered scans across slab segments to compute a fragmentation score and hotspot anchors. Scores are updated into an LRU-friendly index keyed by tenant+segment so eviction decisions can prefer compactable regions. The Spillgate component intercepts candidate spill operations and applies a tenant-aware backoff policy that considers current resident occupancy, historical spill rate, and an adaptive dampening factor to avoid oscillation. Integration with scheduler and kernels: Evictor now exposes locality hints to the dispatcher and batching layer so the scheduler prioritizes fragment-coalescing work on GPU/CPU paths with higher locality, minimizing cacheline churn. The runtime kernel selection path was extended with a small heuristic to choose compacting-friendly kernels for multi-page evictions, improving data movement efficiency. Implementation notes: Changes touch the KV cache manager, evictor, scheduler hints, and metrics. A new config namespace kv.eviction.fragment_sentinel controls scan rate, segment window size, and scoring weights. Spillgate is pluggable and defaults to the conservative policy; operators can configure tenant budgets and an emergency bypass. Testing and benchmarks: Unit tests cover scoring and tenant-budget arithmetic. Integration e2e uses the bench-lab harness with mixed read/write skew and bursty tenant spikes. Bench results on our internal canary cluster show a median p99 tail latency reduction of ~18% under 80/20 hotspot workloads and a 42% reduction in spillback I/O bytes for the same SLOs. Memory residency improved by ~10% due to better coalescing. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag and opt-in config; gradual canary followed by 2-stage ring deploy across Dedicated clusters. Rollback/fallback: if Spillgate reports persistent stalls, system toggles to passive mode which preserves current eviction behavior. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (ENG-4721) referenced - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Benchmark harness runs and baseline comparisons - [x] Runtime flag + config defaults - [x] Observability: metrics, traces, dashboards Notes: This is targeted at short-term wins for production workloads without major refactors to the allocator. Follow-ups planned include a tenant-prioritized compaction backgrounder and adaptive scan-rate learning from workload telemetry.

review_thread: Miguel Santos (review): Could you add a histogram for fragment-score distribution so we can track regression trends? Also request a small test for jitter correctness.
Asha Patel (author): Added histogram metrics fragment_score_bucket and a jitter unit test that asserts non-deterministic scan windows. Bench numbers appended to PR description.
Linus Becker (review): Approved after nit fixes on logging and a comment to avoid expensive atomic ops in hot paths.
Erin Zhao (review): Requested that we add a temporary runtime metric for spillgate_bypass_count during canary; resolved in latest commit.
merge_outcome: Merged by squash after approvals. No conflicts. Canary verified. Deployed to canary clusters on 2026-02-18 and promoted to main fleet 2026-02-20.
release_notes: Introduce Fragment Sentinel scanner and Spillgate backpressure controller to reduce KV cache fragmentation and spillback I/O. Expected improvements: lower p99 latency, fewer cold spills, and better tenant fairness. Feature is behind runtime flag kv.eviction.fragment_sentinel and configurable via kv.eviction.spillgate.*.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature gradually. Observe metrics: fragment_score_bucket, spillgate_hold_ratio, spillgate_bypass_count, tenant_residency_ratio. Default conservative policy is safe for most clusters. If spills stall, toggle kv.eviction.spillgate.mode=passive and contact engineering.
benchmarks_summary: Under mixed skewed workloads on m60 canary: p99 latency -18%, spillback I/O -42%, residency +10%. Bench harness and raw outputs attached to the Linear ticket ENG-4721.
